newsitem.title: USA: CME to open GFX currency arbitrage January 23.
newsitem.headline: CME to open GFX currency arbitrage January 23.

text.p: The Chicago Mercantile Exchange said Thursday it would officially open trading January 23 in its GLOBEX Foreign Exchange Facility (GFX), a currency arbitrage unit.
At startup, GFX's eight salaried traders will make two-way markets in sterling, marks, yen and Swiss francs and offer requests-for-quotes in Canadian and Australian dollars.
GLOBEX is an electronic trading system owned by the CME, Reuters Holdings Plc and the Marche a Terme International de France. The CME alone owns GFX.
GFX also has a chief dealer and three risk managers.
The CME's team of traders, bankrolled by CME money, will actively post currency futures bids and offers on GLOBEX of between $1 million and $3 million in size.
The traders will hedge their futures exposure in the cash foreign exchange market by simultaneously executing offsetting transactions, CME said.

The CME has said the increased volume it expects to generate on GLOBEX through GFX should trickle down into the currency futures pits and boost turnover there as well. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com))
